_about: Reference dictionary of the PolarizedLithiumSim program: the paper copies committed in refs/ (PDFs tracked in git since 2026-08-25; the EIC Yellow Report as four parts) and the few references without a free copy. Each entry: identifiers, title, where the local file is (';'-separated list for multi-part files; null = no free copy), the important content with equation/figure/page pointers, and where the reference is used in the repository. Search it with `python refs/find_ref.py <keyword>`; `--check` lists the local-copy status, `--fetch` re-downloads missing arXiv PDFs. Facts marked (repo-verified) were checked against the primary source during the dated fact-check passes recorded in plans/01 section 6, plans/06 section 6.5 and the reconstruction-chain report.

cosyn2025-tensor-polarization-options.title: Polarization options in inclusive DIS off tensor polarized deuteron
key_content: Eq. (10): exact spin-1 inclusive cross section for UNPOLARIZED electrons: dsigma/dxdQ2 = pi y^2 alpha^2/(Q^4(1-eps)) [F_UU,T + eps F_UU,L + T_LL(F_UTLL,T + eps F_UTLL,L) + sqrt(2eps(1+eps)) T_LT cos(phi_TL) F_UTLT + eps T_TT cos(2phi_TT) F_UTTT]; the decomposition carries NO double-helicity-flip Delta term (their subject is b1).
Eq. (11c) eps = (1 - gamma^2 y^2/4)/(1 - y + y^2/2 + gamma^2 y^2/4); Eq. (13) gamma = M_d Q/(p_d.q) = 2 x_d M_d/Q; rescaled x = 2 x_d.
Eq. (14): in the deuteron rest frame with q along z, T_LL = t_zz, T_LT cos(phi_TL) = t_xz, T_TT cos(2phi_TT) = t_xx - t_yy (components of the polarization tensor).
Eq. (16): F_UU,L = (1+gamma^2) F2/x_d - 2 F1, F_UU,T = 2 F1.

Eq. (17): relations to HJM b1-b4. (17d) F_UTLT = -(gamma/2x_d)[(1+gamma^2)(b2/3 - b4) + 2b2/3 - 2b3] -> the cos(phi) tensor term is O(gamma). (17e) F_UTTT = -(gamma^2/x_d)(b2/6 - b3/2) -> the cos(2phi) tensor term from b2, b3 is O(gamma^2) (higher twist). Eq. (18) Callan-Gross-like b2 = 2 x_d b1 = x b1.

Eq. (20): axis along the virtual photon (N = N_q) -> T_LL = Q/3, T_LT = T_TT = 0 (only two tensor SFs enter: the clean choice for b1/A_zz). Eq. (22): axis along the electron beam (N = N_e) -> T_LL = (3cos^2 theta_q - 1)Q/6, T_LT cos(phi_TL) = -sin(2theta_q) Q/4, T_TT cos(2phi_TT) = (1 - cos 2theta_q) Q/4, theta_q = angle between q and the beam in the target rest frame.
Eqs. (25)-(27): Bjorken limit A_T = -(2/3) b1/F1 (the HERMES extraction relation). Reference gamma values: 0.66 at x = 0.5, Q2 = 2 GeV2; 0.30 at Q2 = 10 GeV2.
Fig. 6: at Q2 = 2 GeV2 the higher-twist b3, b4 are not negligible in the tensor asymmetry and are larger for polarization along the photon direction; they decrease with Q2.
Target context: JLab b1 experiment, DNP ND3 target, 5 T magnet with +-35 deg bore, longitudinal field planned; running with a longitudinal field creates theta_q != 0.
used_in: reports/reconstruction_chain_report.template.html section 2 (Harmonics from the tensor structure functions at finite gamma)
cosyn2025-tensor-polarization-options.repo_usage_note: At the sweet spots gamma^2 <= 0.023, so the b-type leakage into the cos 2phi' amplitude is ~gamma^2 (b1/F1)/6 ~ 4e-4, <= 3% of the Delta amplitude; the O(gamma) cos phi' term is orthogonal to the cos 2phi' fit.

mantysaari2024-polarized-deuteron-imagin.title: Spatial imaging of polarized deuterons at the Electron-Ion Collider
key_content: Eq. (9) (repo-verified from the full text): d^2sigma/(dPhi d|t|) = dsigma/d|t| (1/2pi)[1 + 2 sum_{n>=1} a_n(|t|) e^{i n Phi}] -> the cos(2Phi) modulation COEFFICIENT is 2 a_2, not a_2.

Phi is 'the angle between the produced vector meson and the polarization direction of the deuteron' (in photoproduction the vector-meson transverse momentum is the momentum transfer, i.e. the recoil azimuth); only even n appear (Eqs. 7-8 densities).

'the longitudinal and transverse polarizations are defined in the gamma*d center-of-momentum frame... When Q2 > 0 ... a Lorentz transformation is required from the lab frame to this frame, which would mix the polarization states' (the O(gamma) mixing absorbed by covariant azimuth definitions).

Fig. 4 (digitized in evgen/polligen/coherent.py MANTYSAARI_A2_DEUTERON, x_P = 1.7e-3, transverse polarization): a_2(m=0) = +0.08/+0.15/+0.30/+0.43 and a_2(m=+-1) = -0.04/-0.08/-0.17/-0.28 at |t| = 0.05/0.1/0.2/0.3 GeV^2; a_2(0) ~ -2 a_2(+-1); cos(2Phi) dominates at |t| < 0.5 GeV^2.
Fig. 2: for jz = +-1 the |t| distribution becomes flatter from Phi = 0 to pi/2, opposite for jz = 0 (the D-wave-deformed density modulates the diffractive slope).

Effective transverse radius from a fit dsigma/dt ~ exp(-B_D|t|) within 0 < |t| < 0.3 GeV^2, R = sqrt(2 B_D); Fig. 5: R(Phi) with period pi, jz = +-1 peaks at Phi = 0, jz = 0 dips at Phi = 0; longitudinal polarization shows no Phi dependence.
Slightly increased gluon saturation effects for longitudinally polarized deuterons (ratio of coherent rho cross sections).
mantysaari2024-polarized-deuteron-imagin.repo_usage_note: Money plot 6 injects a_2 as the cos 2phi coefficient and is conservative by x2; money plot 6R injects c_2 = 2 a_2 in the RECOIL azimuth beta = phi_t - phi_S.

zeus2009-leading-protons-lrg.title: Deep inelastic scattering with leading protons or large rapidity gaps at HERA
key_content: Sec. 10.2 (repo-verified): dsigma/dPhi ~ 1 + A_LT cos(Phi) + A_TT cos(2Phi), Phi = angle between the positron and proton scattering planes in the gamma*p frame; for 0.0002 < x_P < 0.01: A_LT = -0.036 +- 0.036 (stat) +0.016/-0.014 (syst), A_TT = -0.030 +- 0.037 +0.022/-0.006; for 0.01 < x_P < 0.1: A_LT = +0.051 +- 0.024 +0.012/-0.011, A_TT = -0.010 +- 0.024 +0.010/-0.009 -> consistent with zero (Figs. 8-9, Tables 3-5); Q2 > 4 GeV2 and an 18 cm RCAL radial cut used for the Phi analysis.

LPS: t resolution sigma(t)/t = 0.14 GeV/sqrt|t| dominated by the angular spread of the HERA proton beam; Phi resolution ~0.2 rad; longitudinal momentum-fraction resolution ~0.5%, transverse-momentum resolution ~5 MeV from the detector; the effective pT resolution was dominated by the intrinsic transverse-momentum spread of the proton beam at the IP, ~45 MeV horizontal and ~100 MeV vertical (factor-2 anisotropy); LPS acceptance ~2% for x_L > 0.98 rising to ~10% at x_L = 0.9; stations S1-S6 at 23.8-90.0 m; analysis t range 0.09 < |t| < 0.55 GeV2.
Eq. (5): t = -pT^2/x_L - (1-x_L)^2 M_p^2/x_L with pT relative to the incoming beam direction.

t-slope: b = 7.0 +- 0.3 GeV^-2 (0.0002 < x_P < 0.01), 6.9 +- 0.3 (0.01 < x_P < 0.1), no Q2 dependence -> soft process; extrapolation to 0 < |t| < 1 GeV2 with b = 7.0 roughly doubles the cross section.

M_X from calorimeter+tracking energy-flow objects, and from the LPS as M_X,LPS^2 ~ [1 - x_L(1+x)] W^2; beam-halo overlap removed with E + p_z(CAL + LPS) < 1860 GeV; LRG sample x_P < 0.02 is >~ 90% diffractive.
Kinematic coverage: 2 < Q2 < 120 GeV2 (LPS), 40 < W < 240 GeV, 2 < M_X < 40 GeV, x_P < 0.1; Pomeron intercept extraction (Sec. 10.5).
zeus2009-leading-protons-lrg.repo_usage_note: u1 = 0.05, u2 = 0.02 in the coherent pseudo-experiments sit at the 1-sigma edge of these bounds; the HERA 45/100 MeV anisotropy is the precedent for the cutout-aspect concern.

nikolaev1998-azimuthal-asymmetry-ddis.journal: (preprint, 1 Dec 1998; IKP Juelich / Landau Institute / Virginia Tech)
nikolaev1998-azimuthal-asymmetry-ddis.title: Azimuthal asymmetry as a new handle on sigma_L/sigma_T in diffractive DIS
key_content: Eq. (1): Q2 y dsigma/(dQ2 dy dM2 dDelta2 dphi) = (alpha_em/2pi^2)[(1 - y + y^2/2) dsigma_T + (1-y) dsigma_L + (1-y) dsigma_TT cos(2phi) + (1 - y/2) sqrt(1-y) dsigma_LT cos(phi)] = ... [1 - y^2 R_D/(2(1-y)+y^2) + 2(1-y) A_TT/(2(1-y)+y^2) cos(2phi) + (2-y) sqrt(1-y) A_LT/(2(1-y)+y^2) cos(phi)] -> the y-factors of the u1 (cos phi) and u2 (cos 2phi) terms used in the repo.
Eq. (2): A_LT = F_LT/(F_T + F_L) = rho_LT/(1 + R_D); Eq. (3): R_D = rho_LT/A_LT - 1; the ratio rho_LT = F_LT/F_T is claimed model independent for beta >~ 0.9 (aligned-jet dominance).

pQCD predicts R_D = sigma_L^D/sigma_T^D >~ 1 for beta >~ 0.9 (higher-twist sigma_L^D dominance), vs R ~ 0.2-0.3 in inclusive DIS; the LT interference is an s-channel helicity non-conserving effect; Eqs. (5)-(8) give the q-qbar excitation amplitudes.

pronyaev1998-forward-cone-lt.title: The forward cone and L/T separation in diffractive DIS
key_content: Eq. (1): same decomposition as Nikolaev-Pronyaev-Zakharov with cos(phi) prefactor (2-y) sqrt(1-y) and cos(2phi) prefactor (1-y); phi = angle between the (e,e') and (p,p') scattering planes.

Eq. (7): R_LT/T = F_LT/F_T = (p_perp/Q) 12 beta^3 (2 - 3beta)/[(1-beta)(3 + 4beta + 8beta^2)] (model independent; sign change at beta = 2/3). At the repo's coherent kinematics (beta ~ 0.5, pT/Q ~ 0.2) this gives A_LT ~ 0.03.
Eqs. (4)-(5): hardness scale Q2bar = (k^2 + m_f^2)/(1 - beta); diffraction cone B_D = Delta B_aX + Delta B_pY + Delta B_int with a rise of B_T from the exclusive limit to the continuum M2 ~ Q2.

key_content: Eq. (2): F2^D(4)(beta, Q2, x_P, t) = beta Q^4/(4pi alpha^2 (1 - y + y^2/2)) dsigma_diff(gamma*p)/(dbeta dQ2 dx_P dt) (dimension GeV^-2); integration over t gives F2^D(3).

jentsch2023-epic-far-forward-dis.journal: Talk, DIS 2023 (30th International Workshop on Deep-Inelastic Scattering), Michigan State University, 27-31 March 2023
jentsch2023-epic-far-forward-dis.title: Far-Forward Detectors and Physics with ePIC @ the EIC
authors: A. Jentsch (on behalf of the ePIC Collaboration)
key_content: Slide 11 acceptance table: ZDC theta < 5.5 mrad (eta > 6); Roman Pots (2 stations) 0.0* < theta < 5.0 mrad (lower bound depends on optics); Off-Momentum Detectors (2 stations) 0.0 < theta < 5.0 mrad; B0 5.5 < theta < 20.0 mrad (4.6 < eta < 5.9). Far-forward means theta < 2.1 deg (~37 mrad).

Slide 15 Roman Pots: 500 um pixelated AC-LGAD sensors, 'potless' design with thin RF foils, sensor planes 25.6 cm x 12.8 cm (modules 3.2 cm) arranged AROUND A HORIZONTAL SLOT through which the beam passes; two stations 2 m apart with two layers each; detector directly in vacuum (impedance studies); generic R&D for adaptive (ML) reconstruction.
Slide 16 OMD: horizontal Roman-Pot-style sensors; protons 123.75 < E < 151.25 GeV (45% < x_L < 55%), 0 < theta < 5 mrad; 'even more challenging reconstruction ... extreme orbit path in the magnets'.
Slide 12/14 B0: MAPS (3 layers) + AC-LGAD (1 layer), PbWO4 EMCAL or Si preshower; tracking resolution demonstrated in stand-alone simulations.

Slide 21/23 ZDC: 60 x 60 x 168 cm, PbWO4 crystal layer + W/Si (12 planes) + Pb/Si (22) + Pb/scintillator (30), 30 m from the IR, acceptance +4.5/-5.5 mrad (aperture limits), position resolution ~1.3 mm at 40 GeV, meets the Yellow Report photon and neutron energy-resolution requirements.

Slide 19 (detector resolution only): Delta pT/pT ~ 0.5-1.5% for Roman Pots at 275 and 100 GeV/c, ~1% B0 at 41 GeV/c, ~2% B0 at 100 GeV/c, OMD ~0.4-1.5%; 'Roman Pots/OMDs suffer from additional smearing due to improper transfer matrix reconstruction'.

Slide 20 (detector + beam effects: angular divergence, crossing angle, crab rotation/vertex smearing): Roman Pots at 275 GeV/c Delta pT/pT ~ 0.09 at pT = 0.45 GeV falling to ~0.04 at 1 GeV (i.e. Delta pT ~ 40 MeV, roughly constant); at 100 GeV/c ~0.10 at 0.15-0.2 GeV falling to ~0.065 at 0.4 GeV; OMD (x_L ~ 0.5) ~0.15 at 0.13 GeV to ~0.06 at 0.4 GeV; B0 at 100 GeV/c ~0.04 at 0.6 GeV to 0.02 at 1.9 GeV -> 'Beam effects the dominant source of momentum smearing!'

maple2024-epic-tracking-inclusive-dis-se.title: Tracking and Inclusive DIS reconstruction with the ePIC detector at the EIC
key_content: Slide 40: inclusive kinematics from two of the four measured quantities D = {E_e, theta_e, delta_h, pT,h}, delta_h = sum_HFS E_i(1 - cos theta_i) (the E - p_z sum), pT,h the HFS transverse momentum; resolutions depend on the event's (x, Q2), detector acceptance/resolution, and radiative processes.

Slide 42 (ePIC 18x275 map, best method for y with marker size = y resolution 25/10/5/1%): electron method at high y, Sigma method in the middle, DA method along the y = 0.01 edge with ~25% markers; 'Resolution throughout phase space allowing 5 (log) bins per decade in x and Q2'; 'Coverage driven by acceptance: 0.01 < y < 0.95, Q2 > 1 GeV2'; 'Lower y accessible -> however it's easier to rely on overlap between data at different sqrt(s)'; 'No single method wins everywhere!'

Slide 43: Bayesian kinematic fit (KF) of all 4 measured quantities for lambda = {x, y, E_gamma} with a prior P0 ~ (1 + (1-y)^2)/(x^3 y^2) x (1 + (1 - E_gamma/E0)^2)/(E_gamma/E0); posterior by Metropolis-Hastings, global mode.

Slide 44 (smeared EIC pseudodata, Djangoh 18x275, Q2 > 1 GeV2): sigma(theta_e) = 0.1 mrad, sigma(E_e)/E = 11%/sqrt(E) (+) 2%, sigma(delta_h)/delta_h = 25%, sigma(pT,h)/pT,h = 25% (repo-verified 2026-08-25).

Slide 45: Delta y/y per method in y bins 0.01-0.05, 0.05-0.1, 0.1-0.2, 0.2-0.5, 0.5-0.8: in 0.01 < y < 0.05 the Sigma/JB/DA/KF methods give roughly Gaussian widths ~0.2-0.3 while the electron method is flat (unusable); at y > 0.2 the electron method and KF are narrowest.

Slide 47 (fully simulated ePIC, Pythia8 NC DIS, Craterlake 23.12.0, Q2 > 100 GeV2, electron from tracking, 0 <= eta <= 0.5): parametrized resolutions sigma_E = 0.055 p (+) 0.45 (Delta p/p in %, A p (+) B with A = 0.055, B = 0.45), sigma_theta = 72/pT (+) 2.8 mrad, sigma_delta_h = 0.25 delta_h, sigma_pT,h = 0.25 pT,h.

Slide 48: full ePIC simulation: 'KF gives comparable y resolution to electron method at high y; loses at low y to DA method'; in 0.01 < y < 0.05 DA is the narrowest, Sigma/JB broad with tails, electron flat. Slide 50: adding an HFS correlation term (width ~8%) recovers the KF at low y (comparable to DA).

Slide 51: ISR energy from the E - p_z conservation Sigma_total = 2E_e,beam (the relation implicit in the Sigma method); slides 52-56, 65: KF on H1 2003/04 data+MC (0.01 < y_eSigma < 0.6, Q2 > 200 GeV2) with sigma(theta_e) = 4 mrad, sigma(E_e)/E = 11%/sqrt(E) (+) 1%, sigma(delta_h)/delta_h = 13.5%, sigma(pT,h)/pT,h = 54%/sqrt(pT,h) (+) 4%; ISR energy reproduced within 30% for E_gamma > 3-4 GeV.

Slides 27-28, 37: ePIC tracking momentum and pointing resolution within reach of the Yellow Report targets except at the largest |eta|; backward momentum requirement still challenging ('high resolution EM calorimetry in this region may provide better reconstruction').
maple2024-epic-tracking-inclusive-dis-se.repo_usage_note: Source of the 25% hadronic-y resolution default and of the 0.01 < y < 0.95 / energy-overlap coverage rule.

athena2022-detector-proposal.title: ATHENA detector proposal -- a totally hermetic electron nucleus apparatus proposed for IP6 at the Electron-Ion Collider
key_content: Sec. 3.1 (PDF p. 50-51, printed p. 44-45): 'The electron-only method performs best over most of the kinematic phase space and will be used for NC DIS measurements at all but the lowest y values... At the lowest y values, the electron method resolution degrades like 1/y. Here, the ability of ATHENA to reconstruct the overall hadronic final state with good resolution can be exploited using the e-Sigma or Double Angle (DA) methods, to ensure high quality measurements for y <~ 0.1, leading to high quality reconstruction at high x... The resolution with the JB method is at the 20-30% level throughout the kinematic range' (repo-verified 2026-08-25).

Fig. 22 (18 x 275 GeV, FullSim): best reconstruction method for y over the (x, Q2) plane with marker size = y resolution (25/10/5/1%): DA (orange) along the y = 0.01 edge with ~25% markers, e-Sigma (green) at low-to-mid Q2 and y ~ 0.02-0.1 with ~10% markers, electron (blue) elsewhere with 5-1%.

Binning/coverage: Q2 > 1 GeV2, y < 0.95 (clean electron ID), y > 0.01 'to ensure that the kinematic variables can be sufficiently well reconstructed (Fig. 22)'; five logarithmic bins per decade in x and Q2; one year per beam-energy combination; HERA point-to-point systematics 1.5-2.5% depending on y.
Table 5 electron-ID efficiency anchors (used by fastsim/scripts/money_delta_20260729.py and reco.eps_eid, via the ATHENA/ECCE tables).

arratia2022-dnn-dis-kinematics.title: Reconstructing the Kinematics of Deep Inelastic Scattering with Deep Learning
key_content: Table 1: formulas of all classical methods from three of the five quantities {E0, E, theta, Sigma, gamma}: electron, DA, hadron (JB), ISigma, IDA, E0ESigma, E0thetaSigma, thetaSigmagamma, double energy (A4), ESigmaT, E0ET, Sigma, eSigma (Sigma = sum_HFS(E_i - p_z,i); Sigma_e the electron's E - p_z; T the HFS transverse momentum).

Setup: Rapgap 3.3 e+p at E0 = 18 GeV, Ep = 275 GeV through the Delphes fast simulation of ATHENA, restricted to Q2 > 200 GeV2; electron = highest-pT track with pT > 5 GeV, EM fraction > 0.8, isolation < 0.2; HFS from energy-flow candidates; Djangoh 1.4 for prior dependence; H1 full simulation (Rapgap 3.1, Geant3, HERA-II) for the demonstration.

Fig. 5 (ATHENA fast simulation, RMS of reco/gen vs generated y, ratio within 0-2): y resolution at y -> 0.05: electron ~0.3, hadron (JB) ~0.17, DA ~0.15, ISigma ~0.13, DNN ~0.05; at y = 0.2: electron ~0.10, DA/ISigma ~0.10, hadron ~0.17; x follows y at low y (electron ~0.3 at y -> 0.05); Q2 resolution: electron ~0.03-0.07, DA/ISigma ~0.05-0.1, hadron 0.15-0.35; the electron method's mean of y/y_gen is biased to 1.12 at the lowest y (repo read-off 2026-08-25).

Sec. 5 'Impact of further acceptance and resolution effects at low y': 'At low y, the HFS-based methods perform better than the electron method... the HFS momentum balance Sigma goes to zero as y goes to zero... Sigma at low y [is] especially sensitive to resolution effects or efficiency losses in the central part of the detector or fake components from calorimetric noise'; the Delphes fast simulation lacks calorimeter noise and edge effects; an ad-hoc Landau noise (mu = 0, sigma = 0.05 GeV per HFS momentum component) brings the fast simulation closer to the H1 full simulation at y <~ 0.15 (Fig. 11).

Fig. 8-9 (H1 full simulation): DNN yields the smallest RMS and is bias-free; at low y the DNN improves y and x substantially over electron and DA; the H1 selection required 45 < Sigma + Sigma_e < 65 GeV to suppress ISR.

aggarwal-caldwell2022-kinematic-fitting.title: Kinematic fitting of neutral current events in deep inelastic ep collisions
key_content: Bayesian kinematic fit of the DIS scaling variables using all measured quantities, with informative priors; better resolution than the electron and double-angle methods and an estimate of the undetected ISR photon energy; demonstrated on a NC ep sample at sqrt(s) = 318 GeV with Q2 > 400 GeV2 (HERA kinematics). The method applied to ePIC in the Maple 2024 seminar.

pecar-vossen2022-sidis-ml-reconstruction.title: Reconstruction of event kinematics in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering using the hadronic final state and machine learning
key_content: EIC SIDIS reconstruction of the virtual-photon axis (p_h perp, phi_h) with a particle-flow network vs electron, JB and DA methods; Figs. 4-5: 'HFS methods surpass electron method for very low y, while PFN equals or outperforms electron method for all y'; cites the Yellow Report / ATHENA fast-simulation method comparisons.

diefenthaler2022-deeply-learning-dis.title: Deeply Learning Deep Inelastic Scattering Kinematics
key_content: DNNs trained on ZEUS simulated data to reconstruct Q2 and x, combining the inputs/outputs of three classical methods; 'sufficiently surpass all classical reconstruction methods on most of the kinematic range'. HERA-based (not EIC).
Local copy: arXiv 2108.11638 (EPJ manuscript, 16 pages).
